Computing the necessary derivatives, we get f(x)=1+x3=(1+x)1/3f(0)=(1+0)1/3=1f′(x)=(13)(1+x)−2/3f′(0)=13(1+0)−2/3=13f″(x)=(−23)⋅(13)(1+x)−5/3=−29(1+x)−5/3f″(0)=−29(1+0)−5/3=−29f‴(x)=(−53)⋅(−29)(1+x)−8/3=1027(1+x)−8/3f‴(0)=1027(1+0)−8/3=1027.

Therefore, the Maclaurin expansion is

1+x3=(1)+(13)x+(−29)x22!+(1027)x33!+⋯=1+x3−x29+5x381+⋯.
